About the tune

  • Music (1917): J. E. Hawes (1862–1933)

Metre: 8.8.8.9 +.9.9.8.9.

Melody from the Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (CCEH, public domain); tune ARE YOU COMING by J. E. Hawes (1862–1933). The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Are You Coming

What is the doh of Are You Coming?

In this version, in E major, doh is E. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Are You Coming start on?

It starts on s (B in E major), a pickup before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

What words can be sung to Are You Coming?

Are You Coming is in the metre 8.8.8.9 +.9.9.8.9: lines of 8, 8, 8, 9,, then, 9, 9, 8, 9 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Are You Coming in the public domain?

Yes. J. E. Hawes died in 1933; the tune was first published in 1917. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
